title: Maximum Width Ramp
summary: In an integer array nums, identify pairs (i, j) where i < j and nums[i] is less than or equal to nums[j].
statement: In an integer array nums, identify pairs (i, j) where i < j and nums[i] is less than or equal to nums[j]. The width of a ramp is the difference between j and i. Return the largest width of any ramp found in nums, or 0 if no ramp exists.
constraints: A ramp is i<=j with nums[i]<=nums[j].
hints: Only indices establishing a new prefix minimum can be optimal left endpoints.
Store those in a decreasing stack, then scan right endpoints backward.
Pop every candidate whose value is <= current right value and update width.
The backward scan gives each popped left index its farthest feasible right endpoint.
editorial: The backward scan gives each popped left index its farthest feasible right endpoint.

tests.explanation: Indices 0 and 5 form the maximum width five.
